Finally, because the incumbent SAF pathways such as HEFA, ATJ, and FT-SPK have already achieved approval and various levels of commercial deployment, MTJ—as other emergent pathways—must show a clear value add relative to the other pathways to spur a new wave of investment. For these reasons, MTJ remains a promising but largely pre-commercial pathway. 2.1.2.2 Power-to-Liquids The final emerging pathway discussed herein is PtL. Although across the aviation sector the term is commonly used to describe specifically FT-based e-kerosene, PtL is a catchall term for the family of conversion pathways that transform CO , H O, and low-carbon electricity into liquids 2 2 and fuels (Figure 15). The key defining features of PtL, as the name suggests, are pathways whose carbon is sourced from CO and whose energy input is electricity, independent of the 2 downstream conversion technology used. These downstream conversion technologies can directly interface with electrons through processes like CO electrolysis, plasmas, and microbial 2 electrosynthesis; or indirectly through reactions with intermediate electricity-derived energy carriers like artificially generated light or H derived from alkaline, proton-exchange membranes 2 (PEMs), or solid oxide electrolyzer cells. (2024) PtL is attracting growing interest as a pathway to SAF because it addresses several fundamental limitations of biomass-based pathways while also providing opportunities for improved efficiency and energy security. First, PtL does not rely on agricultural feedstocks, waste lipids, or land-dependent biomass resources, offering a scalable pathway unconstrained by biomass growth rates or availability, wholly avoiding the “food versus fuel” societal issue. Further, PtL is well 20 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. positioned to leverage future expansion of the renewable electricity market which, when paired with modular-designed electrolyzers for producing CO or H , unlocks a myriad of potential 2 siting opportunities in regions with abundant wind, solar, or other renewable resources. Finally, because its carbon originates from CO and its energy input is low-carbon electricity, PtL has 2 potential environmental advantages where its life cycle emissions have the potential to approach net zero when paired with direct air capture and fully renewable power, offering pathways for improved efficiency and energy security. Despite its long-term strategic importance to supplying the expanding aviation market, PtL SAF faces substantial challenges to achieving meaningful mainstream deployment. The most significant barrier is the required energy intensity and consequent cost. Specifically, whereas petroleum and biomass feedstocks start with C-H chemical bonds and some intrinsic energy content, CO is highly stable, contains no inherent energy (i.e., heating value), and comprises 2 mostly oxygen by weight (~73 wt %). Therefore, PtL processes require enormous energy input to deoxygenate and elevate the energetic properties of the CO feedstock into something more 2 resembling a fuel.
